artifacts.summary: 5-phase loop-guard operational-staleness detector added to skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md Stage 2, documented in orchestrator-runtime-files.md, proven by a 28-assertion fixture suite; one pre-existing check-extension-docs.sh drift reasoned-excluded.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added an OR-combined operational-staleness detector (max_cycles drift, plan_version drift, 7-day mtime backstop) to skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md's Stage 2 loop-guard resume path, archiving a tripped guard and its co-archived churn-state file aside with a loud named notice before falling through to the unmodified fresh-init branch at cycle 0. Recorded the decision, thresholds, and anti-session_id defense in orchestrator-runtime-files.md, and proved the behavior (including the explicit ordinary-cross-turn-resume negative case) with a new 9-fixture, 28-assertion test suite wired into manifest.json.

memory_candidates.content: For an orchestrator loop-guard-style resume file whose read site trusts any syntactically valid file unconditionally, a session_id-equality gate is the wrong staleness signal because the session_id is regenerated on every invocation regardless of whether work progressed -- it flags 100% of legitimate conversational resumes. Prefer OR-combined signals that are invariant across an ordinary resume but change when the guard is genuinely superseded: a schema/version constant drift (e.g. a MAX_CYCLES-style constant baked into the skill file), a lineage drift (e.g. the latest-plan basename the guard last observed vs. the live latest plan), and an mtime-age backstop generous enough to exceed any plausible resume gap. On detection, archive the stale file aside (never delete) with a loud named notice identifying which signal tripped, then let the pre-existing fresh-init branch reinitialize naturally by placing the detector as a fall-through gate before that branch rather than restructuring it in place.

When check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R line_count check fails on multiple entries after an implementation task, diff each failing file's line_count mismatch against the commit immediately preceding the task's first change (git diff <pre-task-sha>..HEAD --stat -- <file>) before assuming the task caused it. Only fix the entry the task's own edit made stale (via the sanctioned generate-context-line-counts.sh maintenance script, scoped by hand-editing index-entries.json if the script itself has no per-entry mode); leave pre-existing, task-unrelated drift alone and record it as a Reasoned Exclusion rather than silently expanding scope to fix everything the check happens to flag.
